tested_scope: One self-contained deterministic local claim/idempotency fixture only. Two writers W1 and W2 share stable effect_identity=E and both begin from the same observed canonical absence. The fixture explicitly assumes, but does not prove the availability of, one atomic canonical single-winner primitive P keyed by E (for example create-if-absent, uniqueness constraint, or compare-and-swap with equivalent single-winner semantics). Both writers submit P(E,payload_hash=H) once. The fixture requires exactly one canonical winner and one conflict/already-exists loser; the loser performs authoritative lookup before any retry and, because the intended payload hash matches H, records duplicate_suppressed rather than mutating again. No lease, external coordinator, richer-mode arbitration, public-source probe, O/downstream state, other-worker state, scheduler mutation, real simultaneous repository write, or optional second leaf was executed.
observations: Given the explicitly assumed atomic single-winner primitive P keyed by stable effect_identity=E, two concurrent writers that both observed absence cannot both commit: one wins and the other receives a conflict/already-exists outcome.

A loser that performs authoritative lookup before any retry and finds the same intended payload hash can terminate as duplicate_suppressed without issuing a second mutation, keeping canonical effect cardinality at exactly one.

The safety result does not require a lease or external coordinator inside the fixture; stable identity plus an atomic canonical single-winner primitive and read-before-retry reconciliation are sufficient for this exact duplicate-suppression branch.
inference: Within this exact deterministic model, atomic uniqueness/CAS on a stable effect identity plus authoritative loser reconciliation is sufficient to prevent duplicate canonical effects under a two-writer same-payload race. This is conditional architecture evidence only: the fixture does not establish that any currently allowed Chat/repository transport actually exposes primitive P, that its conflict signal is authoritative, or that its lookup is linearizable/read-after-write consistent.
unresolved_children: Availability of an atomic single-winner primitive P keyed by stable effect identity on an allowed zero-cost quota-independent transport remains unproven.
Authoritative lookup and read-after-write consistency after the loser conflict remain unproven on real repository/API surfaces.
